root_cause.text: The CAN USB ems_usb driver’s ems_usb_read_bulk_callback() parsed CPC messages using the URB’s transfer_buffer_length (allocated max buffer size) instead of actual_length (bytes actually received) and lacked an upfront per-message header size check, allowing out-of-bounds reads on truncated USB data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN > urb->actual_length)` before casting `ibuf[start]` to `struct ems_cpc_msg`, and changes the end-of-message bounds check from `start > urb->transfer_buffer_length` to `start > urb->actual_length`; the commit message explicitly states that `actual_length` is the real received size and parsing must ensure messages fit within it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before reading a CPC message header to reject malformed USB input and prevent out-of-bounds parsing.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added at the start of the `while (msg_count)` loop in `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback()` to verify that `start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN` does not exceed `urb->actual_length`; if it does, the code logs `"format error\n"` with `netdev_err()` and breaks out of the loop before assigning `msg = (struct ems_cpc_msg *)&ibuf[start]`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the driver from parsing a CPC message header past the end of the received USB bulk buffer when the input is truncated or malformed, avoiding out-of-bounds access and stopping further processing of invalid data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bulk-read message parsing to validate offsets against the URB's actual received length rather than the full transfer buffer size.
intent_record.what: The bounds check in ems_usb_read_bulk_callback() was changed from comparing start against urb->transfer_buffer_length to comparing start against urb->actual_length.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser now validates message traversal against the number of bytes actually received in the URB instead of the full allocated buffer size, preventing it from accepting or walking past unread/invalid data when a short bulk transfer occurs and correctly reporting a format error in that case.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check uses transfer_buffer_length, the allocated buffer capacity, instead of urb->actual_length, the number of bytes actually received. As a result, truncated USB data can still be parsed past the valid received region, enabling out-of-bounds reads.

The code dereferences a CPC message header at the current offset before any upfront check that enough bytes remain for the header in the received data. On truncated input, this can read beyond the valid USB payload.

This reads the message type from the parsed header without first verifying that the header is fully present in the actually received USB data, contributing directly to the out-of-bounds read on malformed/truncated packets.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement forms a CPC message header pointer from the current offset before verifying that enough bytes remain in the actually received USB payload for a full header. On truncated input, this enables out-of-bounds reads.

This dereferences the message header field immediately after constructing the pointer, without an upfront header-length validation against the received data, directly triggering out-of-bounds access on malformed or truncated packets.

This bounds check uses the URB buffer capacity instead of urb->actual_length, so parsing can continue beyond the bytes actually received from USB. That allows truncated data to be treated as valid and contributes to out-of-bounds reads.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 702171adeed3607ee9603ec30ce081411e36ae42
Author: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 16 02:04:20 2009 +0000

    ems_usb: Added support for EMS CPC-USB/ARM7 CAN/USB interface
    
    This patch adds support for one channel CAN/USB interace CPC-USB/ARM7 from
    EMS Dr. Thomas Wuensche (http://www.ems-wuensche.com).
    
    Signed-off-by: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
    Signed-off-by: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is clearly present in ems_usb_read_bulk_callback(), so the function body is sufficient. The root cause says the driver used the URB's allocated buffer size instead of the number of bytes actually received, and lacked an upfront per-message header-size check. In this snippet, parsing begins when only `if (urb->actual_length > CPC_HEADER_SIZE)` is true, then inside the loop it immediately does `msg = (struct ems_cpc_msg *)&ibuf[start];` and accesses `msg->type` before verifying that a full CPC message header is available at `start`. That is the missing upfront per-message header bounds check. Also, after processing each message it advances with `start += CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN + msg->length;` and only then checks `if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)`, which uses `urb->transfer_buffer_length` rather than `urb->actual_length`. Since `transfer_buffer_length` is the allocated max size, truncated USB input can cause reads past received data before this check triggers. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet in this version.

The callback parses messages after only checking `if (urb->actual_length > CPC_HEADER_SIZE)`, then sets `start = CPC_HEADER_SIZE` and enters `while (msg_count) { msg = (struct ems_cpc_msg *)&ibuf[start]; ... }` without first verifying that at least a full CPC message header (`CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN`) is available at `start`. Because parsing of `msg->type` and `msg->length` occurs before ensuring the header lies within the received data, truncated USB data can cause out-of-bounds reads. There is no fix present that validates remaining bytes against `actual_length` before dereferencing each message header/payload.
